subject: Ji et al. (2016)
object: Ji et al. (2016) generated B cell-specific Sel1L-deficient mice (Sel1L-CD19) by crossing Sel1L flox/flox mice on the C57BL/6 background with CD19-Cre mice; the mutant mice were born in a normal Mendelian ratio and appeared healthy with no obvious growth defects, but spleen weights were significantly reduced, the percentage of peripheral B cells in spleen, blood, and lymph nodes was reduced by 60-75%, and absolute numbers of splenic B cells were more than 75% lower than in controls, whereas CD4+, CD8+ T and myeloid cells were not affected. The authors concluded that Sel1L is required for B cell development.

subject: Ji et al. (2016)
object: Ji et al. (2016) found that Sel1L-CD19 mice had a severe developmental block at the transition from large to small pre-B cells: recirculating mature (B220high IgM+) and immature (B220low IgM+) bone marrow B cells were significantly decreased, pro-B cells were slightly elevated, SLC+ CD2- pre-B I and large pre-B cells were twice as numerous, and SLC- CD2+ small pre-B cells were reduced by 50%; apoptotic rates were comparable between cohorts, and neither Sel1L heterozygosity nor CD19-Cre expression alone affected B cell development.

subject: Ji et al. (2016)
object: Ji et al. (2016) showed that the B cell developmental block in Sel1L-CD19 mice was Chop-independent: although BiP and Chop were moderately elevated in large pre-B cells of mutant mice, Chop deficiency in Sel1L-CD19;Chop-/- mice had no impact on the low spleen weight, the paucity of peripheral B cells, or the developmental block at the large pre-B cell stage.

subject: Ji et al. (2016)
object: Ji et al. (2016) reported that expression of the Sel1L and Hrd1 genes was induced around the pre-B cell stage in developing lymphocytes, preceding that of the ER chaperones BiP and Edem1, suggesting a role for Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD in early lymphopoiesis.

subject: Ji et al. (2016)
object: Ji et al. (2016) identified the pre-B cell receptor (pre-BCR) complex, rather than its individual components, as an endogenous substrate of the Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD complex: protein levels of the three pre-BCR components (Igmu, lambda5, VpreB) were dramatically increased and stabilized in pro-/pre-B cells of Sel1L-CD19 mice while transcript levels were unchanged, and loss of either Sel1L or Hrd1 in 70z/3 pre-B cells raised steady-state pre-BCR levels and increased the Igmu half-life from about 60 min to over 120 min with dramatically reduced Igmu ubiquitination.

subject: Ji et al. (2016)
object: Ji et al. (2016) showed that Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD deficiency led to increased ER exit and elevated surface pre-BCR (nearly 3-fold more endoH-resistant Igmu), increased phosphorylation of the downstream effector Syk, and more than 50% more BrdU-positive cycling pro-/pre-B cells in the bone marrow of Sel1L-CD19 mice, with proliferation of lambda5+ large pre-B cells increased more than 2.5-fold; the authors concluded that Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD is required to attenuate pre-BCR signaling by promoting its turnover, and that the mutant mice phenocopy models with gain-of-function pre-BCR signaling.

subject: Ji et al. (2016)
object: Ji et al. (2016) found that the pre-BCR, but not the mature BCR, is a Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD substrate: in LPS-differentiated 70z/3 cells and in mature splenic B cells from inducible Sel1L-knockout (Sel1L-ERCre) mice, the steady-state level, stability, endoH sensitivity and surface IgM of Igmu in the BCR complex were unaffected by Sel1L deficiency, plasma cell differentiation and total IgG were likewise unaffected, and Igmu interacted with Sel1L and OS9 more extensively in pre-B than in mature B cells.

subject: Ji et al. (2016)
object: Ji et al. (2016) demonstrated that ERAD-mediated pre-BCR degradation required BiP but not the unique region of lambda5: depletion of BiP with subtilase cytotoxin SubAB reduced the Igmu-Sel1L interaction and stabilized Igmu protein, whereas a mutant lambda5 lacking the unique region (JC lambda5) did not alter steady-state pre-BCR levels or Igmu half-life and the JC lambda5-containing complex remained an ERAD substrate.

subject: Ji et al. (2016)
object: Ji et al. (2016) noted that global Sel1L-deficient mice are embryonic lethal and that acute Sel1L deletion in adult mice results in pancreatic atrophy and premature lethality, with Sel1L deficiency in adipocytes causing intracellular retention of lipoprotein lipase and hypertriglyceridemia.

subject: Weis et al. (2024)
object: Weis et al. (2024) named a disorder ENDI-agammaglobulinemia (ENDI-A) syndrome. It combines an ERAD-associated neurodevelopmental disorder with onset in infancy (ENDI) with infantile-onset agammaglobulinemia and no mature B cells, leading to frequent infections and early death.

subject: Weis et al. (2024)
object: Weis et al. (2024) reported 5 sibs from 2 consanguineous sibships within a large Roma family from an isolated region of southern Slovakia. All had problems with feeding from birth, with repeated vomiting after eating, failure to gain weight, pallor and gradual cachexia. They also had similar facial dysmorphisms (triangular face, big ears), severe axial hypotonia, global developmental delay, short stature, microcephaly, intellectual disability, and no speech. Three patients could not sit up or hold their heads up, and only patient 4 could sit without support, at age 4.5 years.

subject: Weis et al. (2024)
object: Weis et al. (2024) found that the patients had recurrent severe respiratory infections almost every month, including otitis media, sinusitis, bronchitis and pneumonia, often with respiratory insufficiency caused by food aspiration. Patients 3 and 4 were diagnosed with hearing impairment at 1 year of age, which the authors thought was likely secondary to otitis media. Patients 3, 4 and 5 had no detectable mature CD19+ memory B cells and no circulating immunoglobulins from 12 months of age. Their absolute CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell counts were largely normal, but the CD4:CD8 ratio was reduced.

subject: Weis et al. (2024)
object: Weis et al. (2024) found that a duodenal biopsy from patient 3 showed subtotal villous atrophy (Marsh IIIb enteropathy) with no CD20+ B cells. Patient 4 had COVID-19 with respiratory failure at 7.7 years. The course was prolonged, and no antigen-specific memory T-cell response was detected. All patients died young of infection, sepsis or respiratory failure: patient 1 at 2.9 years, patient 2 at 2 months, and patient 5 at 5.1 years.

subject: Weis et al. (2024)
object: Weis et al. (2024) described further individual findings. Patient 1 developed marasmus and had acute renal failure and pulmonary hypertension. Patient 3 had a ventricular septal defect and epilepsy, with normal myelination on MRI. Patient 4 had leukoencephalopathy on MRI, ptosis, partial papillary atrophy and sideropenic anemia. Patient 5 had leukoencephalopathy, later discrete cortical atrophy, ptosis, micropenis, central hypothyroidism, hypoplastic thymus, hepatopathy and dystrophic nails.

subject: Weis et al. (2024)
object: In 5 affected sibs from 2 consanguineous sibships of a Slovakian Roma family with ENDI-A, Weis et al. (2024) identified a homozygous c.422G>A transition in exon 4 of the SEL1L gene (NM_005065.6), resulting in a cys141-to-tyr (C141Y) substitution. The variant was found by whole-exome sequencing of 2 patients and their parents, assuming recessive inheritance, and was confirmed by Sanger sequencing. It was found in all 5 patients but not in parents or unaffected sibs. It affects a conserved cysteine in the luminal fibronectin type II domain that forms a disulfide bond with Cys168. The authors classified the variant as pathogenic under ACMG criteria but acknowledged that causality could not be firmly established without a knockin mouse.

subject: Weis et al. (2024)
object: Weis et al. (2024) found that a FAR2 variant, R490W, also identified by exome sequencing, did not segregate with disease (in patient 2) and was excluded as causal. Chromosome analysis, SNP array and next-generation sequencing found no other genomic imbalance or variant to explain the phenotypes. aCGH found no large deletions or duplications.

subject: Weis et al. (2024)
object: Weis et al. (2024) reported a female sib (IV-4) who carried 1 C141Y allele. She was born with alobar holoprosencephaly, cleft lip and palate, 'frog' eyes, low-set ears, microcephaly, pterygium colli, polydactyly/syndactyly, anal malformation, contractures, and atrioventricular septal defect with patent ductus arteriosus. She died at 9 days of age of cardiorespiratory failure and had no immune problems.

subject: Weis et al. (2024)
object: Weis et al. (2024) treated patients 3, 4 and 5 with IgG replacement every 4 weeks. Acute infections improved substantially, but chronic respiratory symptoms continued to recur. All 3 eventually deteriorated suddenly with sepsis and multiorgan failure.

subject: Weis et al. (2024)
object: In patient fibroblasts, Weis et al. (2024) found that SEL1L protein was largely undetectable and HRD1 protein was reduced by more than 90%, with normal mRNA levels. Both proteins were unstable, and the ERAD substrates IRE1-alpha and CD147 accumulated. The lectins OS9 and ERLEC1 were decreased. There was no overt unfolded protein response, but ER chaperones were elevated. Biopsies from patients' duodenum also showed reduced SEL1L and HRD1.

subject: Weis et al. (2024)
object: Weis et al. (2024) compared knockin HEK293T cells carrying C141Y with cells carrying the hypomorphic ENDI variants SEL1L M528R, SEL1L G585D and HRD1 P398L. C141Y cells had the lowest SEL1L and HRD1 levels and the highest substrate accumulation, indicating the most severe ERAD dysfunction. Effects were milder than in SEL1L-null cells, suggesting that C141Y is not a complete loss of function. The authors proposed an inverse correlation between ERAD function and disease severity.

subject: Weis et al. (2024)
object: Weis et al. (2024) found that the C141Y variant did not impair formation of the ERAD complex. Disrupting the other FNII disulfide bond (C127Y) had similar effects, whereas deleting the whole FNII domain left ERAD function largely normal. Proteasome inhibition, or deletion of HRD1 but not RNF5, rescued SEL1L levels, and the accumulated mutant SEL1L formed high-molecular-weight aggregates. The authors concluded that the unpaired cysteine causes HRD1-mediated, proteasome-dependent self-destruction of the SEL1L-HRD1 complex.

subject: Weis et al. (2024)
object: Weis et al. (2024) noted that, unlike ENDI patients with hypomorphic SEL1L (G585D, M528R) or HRD1 (P398L) variants who survived into their teens and twenties, patients with the more severe C141Y variant had B-cell immunodeficiency and died early. The authors attributed this to differing degrees of ERAD dysfunction.
